title: Decision making was the bottleneck all along. Productivity is the rate at which you make open-ended decisions, the rate...
teaser: François Chollet: Decision making was the bottleneck all along. Productivity is the rate at which you make open-ended decisions, the rate at which you reduce future paths.
summary: François Chollet argues that the true bottleneck in productivity is not effort, but the speed and effectiveness of decision making. He redefines productivity as the 'rate at which you make open-ended decisions' and the 'rate at which you reduce future paths.'
author: François Chollet
content: Decision making was the bottleneck all along. Productivity is the rate at which you make open-ended decisions, the rate at which you reduce future paths.
